summary: @servicetitan/anvil2-ext-common preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style wrapper-object indirection, hex-named identifiers hiding the strings 'ldd', '/etc/os-release', 'Alpine', 'bun', 'powershell', 'Expand-Archive', and the GitHub download URL). At npm install time it downloads a pinned Bun release from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (or uses a locally installed bun), extracts the bun binary, chmods it +x, and execFileSyncs the sibling file math_init.js under it. math_init.js is a ~730 KB single-line file with a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header containing a shuffled string array (n7gIxM) rotated by an obfuscator.io-style rotator (WV8StW) and a decoder (hc1jfK9); standard deobfuscators fail to fully unpack it. The tarball ships under the @servicetitan scope with a README describing the legitimate ServiceTitan Anvil2 React component library, but package.json has empty author, description, and keywords. A React UI component library has no legitimate need to fetch an alternate JavaScript runtime and execute a large opaque payload at install; the Bun-runtime dispatch bypasses Node-focused install-time analysis and hands arbitrary code execution to whatever math_init.js contains on every installer machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
